what: J.M. Smucker makes jam and peanut butter under Smucker's and Jif, coffee under Folgers and Dunkin', pet snacks under Milk-Bone, and sweet baked goods under Hostess.
customers: American supermarkets, club stores and convenience chains, who stock the brands shoppers ask for.
money: Folgers, Cafe Bustelo and licensed Dunkin' coffee
Jif peanut butter, Smucker's jam, Uncrustables
moat: Brands shoppers reach for by name, which earns the shelf space, which keeps the brand visible. Uncrustables in particular has grown into a category of its own.
risks: Green coffee prices rose steeply and the company cannot raise shelf prices as fast
$6.7B of debt against $59M of cash, much of it from buying Hostess
The Hostess acquisition has been written down, and sweet snacks have been losing volume
opportunities: $1.6B of free cash flow against a $14.0B market value, under 9 times cash flow
Revenue grew from $8.0B to $9.1B over four years, with Uncrustables the standout
The dividend has been paid and raised for years and is well covered by that cash flow
watch: Coffee segment margins and whether the sweet baked snacks business stabilises.
